_readme: THE VECTORS & FORCES FOLD (2026-08-25). forces.json listed 30 maps because it held THREE rival ladders and a junk drawer: the VFM museum (8), the walkable Acts (6), an older Vector*/Forces* ladder (9), and 7 bench/test rooms. The Acts and the museum are not duplicates — they share only 22 of 169 tokens — so both survive, as two SCALES of one ladder (bench and building), the way color kept hand/set/space. Run: python tools/fold_ledger.py --sequence=forces --plan=doc/folds/forces.json --check
_rule: rescue when the token has NO other home in the corpus or is a named piece of a rung; rehome when the registry names another sequence; retire only when the corpus already holds it elsewhere and the piece is furniture, plumbing or a test scene. The 'elsewhere' count in the ledger is the denominator — dark_sphere stands in 308 other maps and science_screen in 212, so forces not placing them is not a loss.

verdicts.3t: retire a utility code sitting in the interactables layer of ForcesComposition — a map bug, not an artifact
verdicts.control_console: retire bench furniture from Console_Test, which was a bench and not a room
verdicts.death_pylon: retire a hazard prop from the props sandbox; hazards are declared in the utilities layer now
verdicts.health_display: retire arena scoreboard furniture; VFM_08_Arena carries its own
verdicts.hits_reset_display: retire arena scoreboard furniture; VFM_08_Arena carries its own
verdicts.throw_ball: retire superseded by the launch room's throwables
verdicts.grab_sphere_point: retire superseded by laser_point on the XL benches (2026)

_labs_are_unlisted: CA_Rules_Lab and Limits_Lab hold five of these benches and appear in NO sequence's map list. They are real homes the curriculum does not name — worth listing, but a separate job from this fold. triangle_curvature_workbench stood only in Console_Test, so it is the one token this fold had to find a room for: NonEuclidean_Spaces, where a triangle's angles stop summing to 180.
